title: Storage Root Lifecycle, Immutable Recording Deletion Safety and Operator UX Closeout
summary: Completes the accepted Stage 13.5 storage-root lifecycle and recording-deletion closeout. Archive-root cleanup and single, selected, camera-wide and bulk recording deletion now use exact root-aware identities, immutable server snapshots, permission revalidation, lease and stale-worker fencing, truthful retry capability and operator-facing progress and result states.
changelog: Unifies single, selected, camera-wide, all-recording and archive-root deletion through shared permission-checked, root-aware operation contracts.
Materializes deletion authority as an immutable NDJSON manifest from one streaming DB snapshot, with atomic publication and SHA-256, item and byte verification.
Executes only exact planned segment, archive-root, relative-path, size and camera identities; new, writing or changed records cannot silently widen an approved deletion scope.
Keeps large deletion plans bounded without arbitrary file-count or byte caps, including plans above 1,000 files and 10 GiB.
Adds renewable operation and scope leases, heartbeat ownership, mutation fencing and stale-worker recovery so expired workers cannot continue deletion.
Revalidates permissions for execution, cancellation and sensitive terminal results, while keeping foreign, missing and already-cancelled plan responses non-disclosing.
Makes archive-root cleanup remove only verified KM VMS recordings and empty owned directories, while preserving foreign files and reporting partial cleanup truthfully.
Provides reason-specific retry modes for immediate retry, refresh, external correction or no retry instead of presenting unsafe generic actions.
Aligns Storage and Records operator dialogs, progress, partial-result details, filters and deletion feedback with the server-side safety contract.
Moves the archive-root deletion running message into the ru, en and zh-CN localization dictionaries.
